# Exactness of a local law derived from history summaries

<!-- Generated by build_result_registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

> Read through a summary, a law takes from each configuration's summary exactly the words that configuration can take, for every configuration, exactly where the configurations the summary merges have the same futures; carrying the futures is not carrying the endpoints.

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

The law read through a summary takes a step from one summary value to another where some configuration with the first takes it to one with the second. From the value of each configuration it takes exactly the words the configuration can take, for every configuration, exactly when the configurations the summary merges can take the same words: the nondeterministic counterpart of a determined law carried through a reduction. For histories, the law extending an admitted history by one move takes, from an admitted history of a prefix-closed language, exactly the courses whose extension is admitted; with the admitted histories as the configurations, the law derived from a summary keeps every finite continuation at every admitted history exactly where admitted histories sharing a code admit the same continuations (proved on the periphery's own definitions; in the core an instance of the first law, not one declaration). Carrying the futures is not carrying the endpoints: the process extending a history by one entry takes every word from every history, so read through any summary it carries the futures; read through the summary marking only [false], one step under false goes from the empty history's code to false, though the empty history extended by false has the code true.

Canonical source: [Readout.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Readout.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- Arbitrary configurations, moves and summary type, a process and a total summary; for histories, a prefix-closed language L. No finiteness, decidability or empty-word membership is required.
- The equivalence quantifies every configuration (for histories, every admitted history); exactness from only one initial value is a different contract.

Histories and summaries describe one unfolding; actual admissibility and the event articulation remain supplied. Construction neither creates actual possibilities nor proves that every process has this finite-word representation.

<a id="检验与边界-validation-and-boundaries"></a>
## Validation and boundaries

Actually compiled with Lean 4.29.1: 6 new theorems and 5 definitions, 11 new empty audits plus 43 inherited empty audits. The first control-summary compilation introduced propext; explicit constructor cases removed it, with the failed record retained. Author counterreview, no independent acceptance.

Finite existential word feasibility only: no endpoint, branch-identity, probability or policy guarantee. An empty L permits vacuous validity without occurrence; the universal assumption-free foundation remains unproved.

- Every word from every history, read through the summary marking only [false]: all continuations are carried, yet one step under false ends at false while the extended history's code is true. [SummaryFutures.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/SummaryFutures.lean)
- Periphery (superseded module): merging histories with distinct continuation profiles produces a witnessed false continuation. [DerivedHistoryLaw.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/deeper/DerivedHistoryLaw.lean)
